name: Referential Density Analysis
description: Analyzes the frequency and complexity of referential expressions (pronouns, demonstratives like 'this/that/these', and synonyms) used to refer back to previously mentioned entities. Humans naturally use complex referential chains to maintain flow and avoid repetitive naming once context is established. AI language models, lacking true cognitive working memory, often 'play it safe' by either over-relying on basic pronouns or clumsily re-stating the full proper noun repeatedly to prevent contextual drift.
mechanism: The algorithm identifies all named entities and tracking nouns within the text. It then maps the coreference chains—how these entities are referred to subsequently. The system calculates the 'Referential Density Score': the ratio of pronouns/demonstratives/synonyms to explicit noun repetitions. Human writing demonstrates high referential density and varied anaphora (using 'the ambitious project', 'it', 'this endeavor' for the same subject). AI text often exhibits a flat density profile, repeatedly using the explicit noun (e.g., 'The company... The company... The company...') to maintain probabilistic safety.
useCase: Effective for analyzing narrative structures, long-form articles, and explanatory texts to detect the mechanistic, overly explicit writing style characteristic of LLMs.
strengths:
• Captures a deep cognitive linguistic feature that is extremely difficult for prompt engineering or basic word-spinning tools to convincingly fake.
• Highly effective on longer texts where human working memory naturally shifts toward pronoun usage.
limitations:
• Less effective on highly technical or legal documents where humans are explicitly trained to repeat formal nouns to avoid any legal ambiguity.
• Short texts do not contain enough entities or subsequent clauses to form a meaningful referential baseline.
parameters:
Analysis: NLP Coreference Chain Extraction
Metric: Ratio of Anaphoric References to Explicit Noun Restatements
Output: 0-100 Referential Rigidity (AI Explicit Naming) Score
accuracy: Moderate to High — 75-82% accuracy. It is a strong secondary metric when combined with Lexical Diversity and Pronoun Usage Patterns.

references.title: Clark, K. et al. (2020). Electra: Pre-training Text Encoders as Discriminators Rather Than Generators. ICLR.
Jurafsky, D. & Martin, J.H. (2024). Speech and Language Processing. 3rd Edition.
